title: Computational Verification and Numerical Precision of Research Foundation Analyzer v6.0 Relative to Commercial Statistical Packages
content: This study evaluates the computational benchmarking and numerical reliability of Research Foundation Analyzer v6.0 against local Python scripting engines (Statsmodels, SciPy, Scikit-learn) and industry-standard statistical software, including SAS Studio Enterprise Edition, GraphPad Prism (version 10.0), and Microsoft Excel. Engineered to address prohibitive licensing costs and data security risks associated with cloud computation, the application executes a Python backend (v3.11.3) via a local Client-Side WebAssembly/Pyodide architecture, ensuring zero remote data transmission and complete user data sovereignty. Algorithmic precision was systematically verified across seven core empirical research scenarios: One-Way ANOVA under Completely Randomized Design (CRD), One-Way ANOVA under Randomized Complete Block Design (RCBD), Two-Way Factorial ANOVA (3×3), Sensory Evaluation under RCBD, multivariate Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Bivariate Pearson Correlation, and 3D Multiple Linear Regression. Across all evaluated parameters—including sum of squares, degrees of freedom, mean squares, F-values, exact probability values (p-values), automated Tukey's HSD letter designations, PCA eigenvalues, component loadings, Pearson coefficients (r), and regression estimators (R², RMSE)—Research Foundation Analyzer v6.0 achieved absolute numerical parity (Δ = 0, representing 100% computational identity) against all reference suites. Partitioning of experimental error, isolation of blocking variance (RCBD, p = 0.0025), and automated post-hoc letterings matched SAS (PROC GLM) and Python scripts with zero divergence. Furthermore, the platform integrates workflow automation through structured Grid Matrix inputs, high-resolution vector graphics (heatmaps, biplots, response surfaces), and instantaneous formatted Microsoft Word (.docx) export. These findings confirm that running scientific Python routines inside a local WebAssembly environment maintains full 64-bit IEEE 754 precision without computational drift, establishing Research Foundation Analyzer v6.0 as an institutional-grade, accessible, and privacy-preserving computational tool for higher education, graduate research, and peer-reviewed scientific publishing.
